body:
Design the fix loop that runs after the CI review. When a review has findings marked "fix", another Claude Code run in CI fixes them and pushes, and the push starts the next review. After three fix rounds, a fourth review runs, and the PR goes to Joe with a "ready for Joe" label.

PR #39 showed the loop needs two limits: a rule for which findings get fixed, and a cap on rounds. It went seven rounds without either, and most of its 36 findings were minor (`research/code-review-evaluation.md`, section 10).

The work to build it is split into #75 (the review agent), #76 (the fix agent), and #77 (the loop).

## Design

- The code review design, `design/code-review.md`, is on the branch `code-review-design`. Section 3 holds the rules for which findings get fixed. Section 4 holds the loop's design, agreed in chat on 2026-10-19.

## Open questions

- ~~Is the code review design finished and merged first, in its own PR, before the loop is built?~~ Settled 2026-10-19 in chat: yes. This issue's PR merges before #75 starts.
- ~~Do the loop's open questions stay in the design doc's section 4.5, or move into this issue?~~ Settled 2026-10-19: they moved here, since CLAUDE.md puts a question an open issue will answer in that issue.
- ~~How does a PR show that it's ready for Joe: a label, or a check result?~~ Settled 2026-10-19 in chat: a "ready for Joe" label (design section 4.6).
- ~~How can the workflow tell that a review ran, when all its commands were blocked?~~ Moved to #75.
- ~~Is a design doc that doesn't match the code above the bar?~~ Moved to #75.
- ~~Does the fixer decide whether a finding is above the bar, or does a separate step decide it?~~ Settled 2026-10-19 in chat: the reviewer marks each finding "fix" or "note", and the fixer gets only the "fix" ones (design section 4.2).
- ~~Does the fixer read the decisions comment?~~ Moved to #76.
- ~~Are the cleanups saved up for a separate pass now and then, so they're fixed without feeding the next review?~~ Moved to #77.
- ~~Should "the PR doesn't do what its task says" be a rule in the bar (design section 3.1)?~~ Settled 2026-10-19 in chat: yes (design section 3.1).
- ~~Which model and effort does the fixer use?~~ Settled 2026-10-19 in chat: Opus 5.5 at `high`, as in Joe's coding sessions (design section 4.5).
- ~~Does a push by Joe reset the count of fix rounds?~~ Settled 2026-10-19 in chat: no (design section 4.6).
- ~~Does the project's auto-add setting put the fixer's new issues in Triage, so the fixer never needs the project board?~~ Settled 2026-10-19 in chat: yes, Joe tested it. The fixer only needs to read and open issues in this repo (design section 4.5).

## Do

- Write the loop's design into `design/code-review.md` section 4.
- Move the review and fix loop guide from `scratch/` to `research/agent-review-fix-loop.md`.
- Open an issue for each piece of the build: #75, #76, and #77.

## Done when

- `design/code-review.md` section 4 holds the design agreed in chat, and #75 to #77 are open.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

Moved from open item 14 in the [open items](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/open-items.md).

When a CI review has findings marked "fix", another Claude Code run in CI fixes them and pushes. The push starts the next review. After three fix rounds, a fourth review runs, and the PR goes to Joe with a "ready for Joe" label.

PR #39 showed the loop needs two limits: a rule for which findings get fixed, and a cap on rounds. It went seven rounds without either, and most of its 36 findings were minor (`research/code-review-evaluation.md`, section 10).

## Design

- The code review design, `design/code-review.md`, is on the local branch `code-review-design`, not pushed yet. Section 3 holds the rules for which findings get fixed.
- Its section 4 holds the loop's design, agreed in chat on 2026-10-19: our own review prompt, findings marked "fix" or "note", a "Set aside" list in the PR description, a review job and a fix job in each workflow run, a cap of three fix rounds, and a GitHub App for the fixer.

## Open questions

- Is the code review design finished and merged first, in its own PR, before the loop is built?
- ~~Do the loop's open questions stay in the design doc's section 4.5, or move into this issue?~~ Settled 2026-10-19: they moved here, since CLAUDE.md puts a question an open issue will answer in that issue.
- ~~How does a PR show that it's ready for Joe: a label, or a check result?~~ Settled 2026-10-19 in chat: a "ready for Joe" label (design section 4.6).
- How can the workflow tell that a review ran, when all its commands were blocked?
- Is a design doc that doesn't match the code above the bar? Agents build from the design docs, so a wrong one leads to wrong code later. The stock review rarely finds these (research doc, section 8.3).
- ~~Does the fixer decide whether a finding is above the bar, or does a separate step decide it?~~ Settled 2026-10-19 in chat: the reviewer marks each finding "fix" or "note", and the fixer gets only the "fix" ones (design section 4.2).
- Does the fixer read the decisions comment? It's doing the implementer's job, so the implementer's reasons may help it, unlike the reviewer.
- Are the cleanups saved up for a separate pass now and then, so they're fixed without feeding the next review?
- Should "the PR doesn't do what its task says" be a rule in the bar (design section 3.1)?
- Which model and effort does the fixer use?
- Does a push by Joe reset the count of fix rounds? The first thought is no.
- Does the project's auto-add setting put the fixer's new issues in Triage, so the fixer never needs the project board?

## Do

- To be written once the open questions are settled.

## Ends in

A PR.

When a CI review has findings, another Claude Code run in CI fixes them and pushes, for at most two or three rounds. A clean review marks the PR ready for Joe.

PR #39 showed it needs two limits. Fix only findings that cause wrong behavior, lost data, or a security hole, and list the rest in the PR comment for Joe. Stop after two fix rounds, since each fix gives the next review new lines to find things in. PR #39 went seven rounds without either, and most of its 36 findings were minor (`research/code-review-evaluation.md`, section 10).

## Design

- A draft code review design, `design/code-review.md`, is on the local branch `code-review-design`, not pushed yet. Its sections 3 and 4 hold the rules for which findings get fixed and for the loop, and section 4.5 holds the loop's open questions.

## Open questions

- Is the code review design finished and merged first, in its own PR, before the loop is built?
- Do the loop's open questions stay in the design doc's section 4.5, or move into this issue?

- To be written once the open questions are settled.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.
